web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: At ₹1,073.10 per share and a ₹24,405 Cr market cap (79.0x TTM earnings), what growth and cash-conversion path has the market already priced in?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a capital-goods manufacturer trades at seventy-nine times trailing earnings while converting negative cumulative free cash flow, the stock price is already discounting five years of flawless execution.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Desk

web_blocks.html: On November 13, 2026, Jyoti CNC Automation closed at ₹1,073.10 on the NSE [1]. That price implies a market cap of ₹24,405 Cr [1]. Adding ₹946 Cr of September 2026 debt puts enterprise value near ₹25,351 Cr [1]. Against TTM consolidated net profit of ₹309 Cr (EPS ₹13.57), the stock trades at 79.0x TTM P/E and 11.4x Price-to-Book [1]. On TTM operating profit of ₹542 Cr, it trades at 46.8x EV/EBITDA [1]. For a builder with negative ₹847 Cr cumulative FCF over FY24–FY26, that multiple prices in years of flawless execution [1].

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Reverse DCF: What Today's ₹24,405 Cr Market Cap Already Assumes

web_blocks.html: A Reverse DCF asks what future cash flows are needed to justify a ₹25,351 Cr enterprise value today. We use an 11.5% cost of capital (WACC) and a 4.5% terminal growth rate. We also credit Jyoti CNC for expanding Rajkot capacity from 6,000 to 16,000 machines and executing its ₹5,082 Cr backlog [3, 23]. Even with those generous assumptions, the implied path is steep:

web_blocks.caption: Reverse DCF Implied Expectations at CMP ₹1,073.10 (EV ₹25,351 Cr | WACC 11.5% | Terminal Growth 4.5%)
rows: Demanding; requires >20% domestic share plus major export ramp
Aggressive; Q2 FY27 consolidated margin was 21.8% due to Huron drag [1, 23]
Unproven; WC days expanded from 181 (FY24) to 234 (FY26) [1]
Positive +65% to +75% FCF/PAT from FY29 onward
Requires capex intensity to drop sharply after ECMS & 16k build
web_blocks.takeaway: To earn an 11.5% annual return from ₹1,073.10, Jyoti CNC must compound sales at ~23% for ten years, hold 25%+ margins, and halve working-capital days.

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Quantitative Peer Comparison: Domestic CNC & Industrial Capital Goods

web_blocks.html: Comparing Jyoti CNC with listed Indian CNC and industrial peers highlights a wide valuation gap [1, 25, 26, 27]. Domestic CNC peer Macpower CNC trades at 53.4x P/E [27]. Proven industrial compounders trade far cheaper: Elgi Equipments sits at 40.6x P/E (22.1% ROCE), and Elecon Engineering sits at 40.7x P/E (20.9% ROCE) [25, 26]. Even Triveni Turbine, with 34.1% ROCE and net cash, trades at 54.3x P/E [26]. Jyoti CNC commands a 45% to 95% P/E premium despite weak cash conversion [1].

web_blocks.caption: JYOTICNC vs. Domestic CNC & Industrial Capital-Goods Peers (Session Cutoff: 2026-11-13)
web_blocks.takeaway: JYOTICNC trades at 79.0x P/E—nearly double Elgi Equipments (40.6x) and Elecon Engineering (40.7x), and 45% above Triveni Turbine (54.3x) despite Triveni's 34.1% ROCE [1, 25, 26].

web_blocks.html: We model three FY28E scenarios for consolidated earnings and exit multiples. Our Base Case assumes Rajkot scales toward 8,000+ annual machines and consolidated revenue reaches ₹3,200 Cr. It assumes 24.5% EBITDA margins and gradual resolution at Huron, yielding FY28E EPS near ₹21.10. Applying a generous 45x multiple gives a Base Case value of ₹950 per share—sitting 11.5% below today's ₹1,073.10 price [1, 23, 26].

Valuation Trigger That Would Change Our View: We would reconsider our valuation rejection only if the stock re-rates below ₹750 (roughly 35x FY28E EPS) alongside two quarters of CFO/PAT above 60%, or if earnings beat our FY28E Base Case by 25%+ without adding debt.

web_blocks.company: Kennametal India & Bharat Fritz Werner Peers (2017–2020 Cycle)
web_blocks.mechanism: During the 2017–2018 domestic capex boom, Indian machine-tool stocks re-rated to 55x–70x trailing earnings on strong order-book stories while inventory and receivable days quietly lengthened.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: When auto and engineering capex paused in FY19–FY20, sales fell 18%–29% and multiples compressed from >55x to 22x–28x, causing 40%–55% peak-to-trough drawdowns.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Paying 79.0x trailing P/E for a cyclical CNC builder with 453 inventory days and ₹946 Cr of debt exposes buyers to both earnings cuts and multiple compression.

book_paragraphs: Now that you and I have completed our price-blind audit of Jyoti CNC's factory floor, order book, working capital, and French subsidiary, let us finally open the market screen and look at what Mr. Market is charging for this business. As of the November 13, 2026 close, Jyoti CNC trades at ₹1,073.10 per share. That gives the company a market capitalization of ₹24,405 Cr and an enterprise value north of ₹25,350 Cr once we add back the ₹946 Cr of borrowings sitting on the September 2026 balance sheet.

Pause and let that number sink in. Against trailing twelve-month consolidated net profit of ₹309 Cr, the market is asking us to pay 79.0 times trailing earnings and 11.4 times book value. Let me ask you a simple question: what kind of business normally commands 79 times earnings? Typically, you pay that multiple for an asset-light software monopoly, a debt-free consumer staple with 40% returns on capital, or an industrial franchise that converts every rupee of accounting profit into free cash flow.

Jyoti CNC is none of those right now. Over the last three fiscal years combined—FY24 through FY26—the company reported ₹803 Cr of accounting net profit, yet generated negative ₹99 Cr of operating cash flow and negative ₹847 Cr of free cash flow. When a capital-intensive manufacturer trades at 79 times earnings while burning cash to fund 453 days of inventory and a massive capacity buildout, the stock price is not reflecting current reality. It is discounting five to ten years of near-perfect execution.

Let us test exactly how much perfection is baked into ₹1,073.10 using a Reverse DCF. At an 11.5% cost of capital and a 4.5% terminal growth rate, justifying a ₹25,351 Cr enterprise value requires Jyoti CNC to compound consolidated revenue at roughly 23% annually for a full decade—taking the top line from ₹2,093 Cr in FY26 to roughly ₹16,500 Cr by FY36—while simultaneously holding 25%+ EBITDA margins and slashing working capital from 234 days down below 110 days. That is a razor-thin tightrope with zero room for a European export-control snag or a domestic auto-capex pause.

Look across the aisle at listed Indian industrial peers and the valuation gap becomes even clearer. Elgi Equipments, a globally competitive air-compressor manufacturer with 22.1% ROCE and clean cash conversion, trades at 40.6x P/E. Elecon Engineering trades at 40.7x P/E with 20.9% ROCE. Even Triveni Turbine—which boasts a 34.1% ROCE, 25.2% ROE, and net-cash balance sheet—trades at 54.3x P/E. Jyoti CNC at 79.0x P/E is priced at a 45% to 95% premium over these proven compounders.

Let us also examine how Jyoti CNC’s enterprise-value-to-EBITDA multiple stacks up against its own cash-flow reality. At an enterprise value of ₹25,351 Cr against TTM operating profit of ₹542 Cr, the market is paying 46.8 times trailing EBITDA. Normally, a capital-goods company trading near 47 times EBITDA is either at a cyclical earnings trough—like LMW at 87.7 times depressed textile-machinery earnings—or it is converting 80% of EBITDA into unencumbered free cash flow. Jyoti CNC is neither at a cyclical trough nor converting EBITDA into cash: TTM operating margins sit near historical highs at 24% to 25%, while pre-tax CFO-to-EBITDA conversion sat at just 34% in FY26 and negative 4% in FY25.

Why does that distinction matter so much to you and me? Because when a stock is priced at 46.8 times peak-cycle EBITDA and 79.0 times trailing P/E, any deceleration in quarterly dispatches or any further working-capital absorption triggers a double whammy: earnings estimates get trimmed at the exact same moment the valuation multiple compresses toward peer levels of 35 to 45 times. Look at our Kennametal India and Bharat Fritz Werner cycle parallel from 2017–2020: when domestic auto and general-engineering capex paused in FY19, machine-tool multiples compressed from over 55x to 25x in less than eighteen months.

Even if we assume Jyoti CNC executes well—ramping Rajkot toward 8,000+ machines in FY27, holding 24.5% consolidated EBITDA margins, and resolving Huron’s French export-control overhang without punitive fines—our FY28E normalized EPS of ₹21.10 at a generous 45x forward multiple only gets us to ₹950 per share. Buying at ₹1,073.10 today means paying upfront for a Base Case that already sits 11.5% below the current market price.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The hardest discipline in institutional investing is separating a genuinely improving industrial franchise from an unforgiving stock price. Jyoti CNC's ₹5,082 Cr order book is real, and its 28% standalone Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin is impressive—but at 79.0x TTM P/E, you are paying upfront for FY30 perfection while absorbing FY26's -₹269 Cr free cash flow deficit.
